# fyne and gtk4 have no errorBoundary emitter. Left to travel on, the boundary
# reached the Go renderer, which walks the same IR from a different angle and
# panics on a statement kind no platform was meant to hand it -- so what a user
# saw was a Go stack trace naming irwalk, about a program it never mentioned.
#
# Declining by name up front is the answer the translator already gives for an
# ordinary component, and it is the same typed error, so `sngl test` reports it
# as a skip for that platform rather than a failure.

! sngl generate --platform=fyne --lang=go --out=fy boundary.sngl
stderr 'component "errorBoundary" has no fyne implementation'
! stderr 'panic'

! sngl generate --platform=gtk4 --lang=go --out=gt boundary.sngl
stderr 'component "errorBoundary" has no gtk4 implementation'
! stderr 'panic'

# The platforms that do implement one are unaffected.
sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --out=ht boundary.sngl
sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --out=bt boundary.sngl
sngl generate --platform=android --lang=kotlin --out=an boundary.sngl

-- boundary.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:app"

component main ui {
    var caught = ""
    errorBoundary(@error(e) { caught = e.message }) {
        button #go(text="Go", @click { error.raise("boom", "") })
    }
    text(value=caught)
}

window {
    main
}
